comments.body:
Root cause CONFIRMED with a purely local repro (no proxy, no network, no timeout).

init decided 'does the remote have a tickets branch?' by reading the LOCAL ref: init.py:367 ran 'git rev-parse --verify origin/tickets', which resolves refs/remotes/origin/tickets in the local object store - not a remote query. A full clone adopts the remote history; a 'git clone --single-branch --branch main' of the SAME repo silently bootstraps a 5-commit orphan, rebar list returns [], and merge-base exits 1. The same purely-local predicate backed the auto-init consent gate (init.py:645), which is why the reporter's FIRST command died with 'auto-init requires an interactive terminal'.

The agent proxy was a PRECONDITION, not the cause: --single-branch, --depth, a refspec-limited mirror, an interrupted fetch, or a branch published since the last fetch all reach the same state.

Authority: docs/architecture.md promises attachment when the branch exists 'locally OR ON origin', automatically, 'even with no TTY', explicitly for CI/agent/headless use. The doc said 'on origin'; the code implemented 'in refs/remotes/origin/'. This is the incomplete implementation of prior bug wet-chair-peg, whose regression test only ever covered the case where the tracking ref happens to be present.

FIX: one shared discriminator init.locate_tickets_branch returning local/tracking/remote/unreachable/none, used by BOTH the mount path and the consent gate. On 'remote' it fetches into the tracking ref with an explicit refspec then mounts; if the branch is known but the fetch fails it FAILS LOUDLY rather than fabricate a divergent store (AC2). 'unreachable' warns and keeps orphan-bootstrap so offline first-time init still works. Only the cheap ls-remote probe is bounded (15s) - the fetch itself is unbounded, which matters for the reporter's 49k-commit branch that needed minutes.

AC3: fsck now reports DIVERGED (no merge-base) as a real issue with a non-zero exit, and no longer mislabels an unrelated orphan history as 'ahead by N commits - push pending' followed by 'no issues found'.

ALSO CONFIRMED, NOT FIXED (out of this ticket's ACs): sync.py:170-173 gates its self-heal on the same missing tracking ref, and a bare 'git fetch <remote> <branch>' under a narrow clone refspec writes only FETCH_HEAD - so the --allow-unrelated-histories union merge at sync.py:96 is unreachable and an ALREADY-divergent store never heals itself. That explains why the reporter's store stayed empty all session. AC3's fsck DIVERGED report is the ticket's chosen remedy for existing divergent stores; making sync auto-heal them is a separate change and should get its own ticket.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`rebar init` (auto-init / `rebar init --silent`) created a **fresh, empty** local
tracker on a new `tickets` branch even though an authoritative `tickets` branch with
real ticket history already existed on the configured sync remote (`origin`). The local
tracker (`.tickets-tracker`) diverged from `origin/tickets`, so every read command
(`rebar list`, `rebar show`, `search`, …) returns an EMPTY store, hiding all existing
tickets. Any writes made now land on the divergent local branch and cannot be
fast-forward-pushed back to `origin/tickets`.

Root contributing factor: fetching the remote `tickets` branch times out
(>100s) through the agent git proxy, so init silently fell back to bootstrapping a fresh
store instead of failing loudly or retrying.

## Impact

- `rebar list --status=open --type=bug` (and all other reads) return `[]` — existing
  work is invisible.
- New ticket events are written to a divergent local `tickets` history that will not
  fast-forward onto `origin/tickets`, risking lost or conflicting events.
- Silent data-hiding: no error is surfaced to the operator; the store simply looks empty.

## Environment

- Remote execution environment (Claude Code on the web), ephemeral container.
- Primary working directory: `/home/user/rebar`
- Platform: Linux 6.18.5
- Checked-out code branch: `claude/open-bugs-list-m4iu76`
- rebar version: `nava-rebar 0.10.1`
- `origin` remote: `http://local_proxy@127.0.0.1:41729/git/navapbc/rebar`
- Outbound git/HTTPS goes through the pre-configured agent proxy.
- No `.venv` was present at session start; `rebar` was not on `PATH`. Bootstrapped with
  `python3 -m venv .venv && make install`.
- Config (relevant): `sync.remote = origin`, `sync.pull = on`, `sync.push = always`.

## Reproduction — exact commands and observed output

1. rebar not installed / not on PATH:

   ```
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   /bin/bash: line 1: rebar: command not found
   $ python3 -m rebar list ...
   /usr/local/bin/python3: No module named rebar
   $ ls .venv
   ls: cannot access '.venv': No such file or directory
   ```

2. Bootstrap env:

   ```
   $ python3 -m venv .venv && make install
   Successfully installed ... nava-rebar-0.10.1 ...
   ```

3. Store reports not initialized, then init produced an EMPTY store:

   ```
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   Error: ticket system not initialized. Run 'rebar init' first (auto-init requires an interactive terminal).
   $ rebar init --silent
   (no output)
   $ rebar list --status=open --type=bug
   []
   $ rebar list                       # all statuses
   []
   ```

4. But a real `tickets` branch exists on `origin`, and it is actively moving (other
   agents writing to it) — two `ls-remote` reads minutes apart returned different tips:

   ```
   $ git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/tickets'
   aa498170daa39767eab3282f505700e30bbed1ea  refs/heads/tickets   # first check
   ...
   $ git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/tickets'
   4b51478a14c150a1032a8b2988d1524bfda1da54  refs/heads/tickets   # minutes later
   ```

5. The local tracker worktree is a FRESH divergent branch (bootstrap commits only, none
   of the remote history):

   ```
   $ git worktree list
   /home/user/rebar               ... claude/open-bugs-list-m4iu76
   /home/user/rebar/.tickets-tracker ... tickets

   $ git -C .tickets-tracker log --oneline -n 6
   37e8b02 chore: add .store-compat.json store-compatibility record (story 21dd)
   ed99e08 chore: add .gitignore for env-id, state-cache, scratch, and reducer cache
   936ec76 chore: add .gitattributes merge=ours for shared mutable root files (epic 97e7)
   a7ad28d chore: add no-op .pre-commit-config.yaml (bug 27d8-b230)
   94e48da chore: initialize ticket tracker
   $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse tickets
   37e8b026cf61e04b651f29b849294f6d549c8210
   ```

   Local tip `37e8b02` shares no history with remote tip `4b51478a` → divergent.

6. Fetching the remote `tickets` branch to reconverge TIMES OUT (reproduced multiple
   times, both from the main checkout and from inside `.tickets-tracker`):

   ```
   $ git -C .tickets-tracker fetch origin tickets      # 100s timeout
   Terminated   (exit 143)
   $ git fetch origin tickets                          # 120s tool timeout
   Command timed out after 2m 0s
   ```

   `rebar fsck` reports the (empty) local store as healthy, so nothing flags the problem:

   ```
   $ rebar fsck
   ensures: 6/6 applied
   authorship: 0 signed, 0 unsigned event(s)
   fsck complete: no issues found
   ```

## Confirmed divergence and fetch-latency (observed this session)

A full (unbounded-timeout) background fetch of `origin/tickets` eventually SUCCEEDED,
which let me quantify both the divergence and the latency that caused the fallback:

- The remote `tickets` branch is large and event-sourced — **49,301 commits**:

  ```
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-list --count origin/tickets
  49301
  ```

- The local auto-initialized tracker and `origin/tickets` share **NO common ancestor**
  (definitively a fresh, divergent store — not a fast-forwardable lag):

  ```
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker merge-base tickets origin/tickets
  (no output; exit 1) -> NO COMMON ANCESTOR (divergent)
  $ git rev-parse origin/tickets      # authoritative
  80ec6ba00f4ce4daef8dada62c8056e003e8ef92
  $ git -C .tickets-tracker rev-parse tickets   # local fresh-init
  dcb0b1ac7ff39999016a7aa73eeef9644b1e0247
  ```

- The branch is **actively written by other agents** — its tip moved four times across
  this single session: `aa498170…` → `4b51478a…` → `80ec6ba…`, etc.

- **Fetch latency is the trigger:** `git fetch origin tickets` was killed at 100s and at
  the 120s tool limit, but the same fetch run WITHOUT a kill-timeout (in the background)
  completed successfully in several minutes. So the branch is reachable; init simply gave
  up (or its bounded fetch timed out) and fell back to a fresh empty store rather than
  waiting/retrying. A bounded init fetch against a 49k-commit branch over the proxy is not
  enough headroom.

## Expected behavior

`rebar init` MUST NOT silently bootstrap a fresh empty store when the configured sync
remote already has a `tickets` branch. It should either:

- fetch/adopt `origin/tickets` as the local tracker's base (the store is non-empty), or
- fail loudly (non-zero exit, clear message) when it cannot reach/fetch the existing
  remote `tickets` branch, instead of falling back to a divergent empty store.

Additionally, the remote-`tickets` fetch through the agent proxy should be made
resilient (retry/backoff, longer timeout) rather than silently abandoned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar init` / auto-init detects an existing `tickets` branch on `sync.remote`
      before creating a new one, and bases the local tracker on it (reads return the
      existing tickets, not `[]`).
- [ ] When the existing remote `tickets` branch cannot be fetched, init fails loudly
      (clear error + non-zero exit) instead of silently bootstrapping a divergent empty
      store.
- [ ] A health check (`fsck`/`validate`) detects and reports a local `tickets` tracker
      that has diverged from `origin/tickets` (no shared history / cannot fast-forward),
      rather than reporting "no issues found".
- [ ] Regression coverage: a test simulates a reachable, non-empty remote `tickets`
      branch and asserts init does not produce an empty divergent store.

## Notes

- Filed per operator request while investigating "show me a list of open bugs" returning
  an empty list.
- Because the local store is currently divergent and the remote fetch times out, this
  ticket may itself be written to the divergent local `tickets` history and may not sync
  to `origin/tickets` until the underlying fetch/reconverge issue is resolved.
